easy.def: To ruin something on purpose.
examples: He tried to sabotage the game.
She sabotaged the plan.
They sabotaged the machine.

more.def: To damage or ruin something on purpose so that it cannot work.
examples: He tried to sabotage the science project.
The villain sabotaged the machine.
Someone sabotaged our plan by hiding the map.

easy.def: A big bag.
examples: I carried a sack.
The sack of potatoes is heavy.
The sack is full of toys.

more.def: A large bag made of strong paper or cloth.
examples: Dad carried a sack of potatoes.
The sack was filled with apples.
She packed her lunch in a paper sack.

easy.def: Holy, or deserving great respect.
examples: The temple is a sacred place.
The book is sacred.
The mountain is sacred.

more.def: Holy, or treated with the greatest respect because it belongs to a religion.
examples: The temple is a sacred place for many people.
The river is sacred in that country.
A sacred book was kept in a special box.

easy.def: Giving up something you like for someone else.
examples: Mom made a sacrifice to buy us shoes.
Giving up your seat is a small sacrifice.
It was a big sacrifice for him.

more.def: Something good that you give up so that someone else can have something better.
examples: Her parents made many sacrifices so she could go to school.
Giving up a day off was a sacrifice for the nurse.
The soldier's sacrifice was honored by the town.

easy.def: To give up something you like for someone else.
examples: I sacrificed my free time to help.
She sacrificed her turn.
He sacrificed his dessert for his sister.

more.def: To give up something you value so that someone else may have something.
examples: The family sacrificed their vacation to pay for the new roof.
He sacrificed sleep to finish the model.
Farmers sacrificed part of their crop to save the village.

easy.def: Not happy.
examples: I feel sad.
It was a sad story.
She is sad.

more.def: Feeling unhappy or causing unhappy feelings.
examples: He felt sad when his friend moved away.
It was a sad movie about a lost puppy.
She was sad because the party was over.

easy.def: A seat on a horse or a bike.
examples: The rider sat in the saddle.
The saddle is leather.
I put the saddle on the horse.

more.def: A seat for a rider on a horse, or on a bicycle.
examples: The rider climbed into the saddle.
The saddle on my bike is too high.
She tightened the horse's saddle.

easy.def: In a sad way.
examples: The boy sadly waved goodbye.
She sadly said no.
The dog looked sadly at us.

more.def: In a way that shows sadness, or unfortunately.
examples: The girl waved sadly as the bus left.
Sadly, the party was canceled.
The dog gazed sadly at the empty bowl.

easy.def: The feeling you have when you are not happy.
examples: I felt sadness when my friend left.
Sadness filled the room.
There was sadness in her eyes.

more.def: The feeling of being unhappy, often because something bad has happened.
examples: He felt sadness when his best friend moved far away.
A feeling of sadness came over her as summer ended.
The movie's ending filled the audience with both joy and sadness.

easy.def: Not in danger.
examples: The kitten is safe in the box.
Wear a helmet to stay safe.
It is safe to cross now.

more.def: Free from danger or harm, or not likely to cause harm.
examples: A helmet keeps your head safe when you ride a bike.
It is safe to swim here because the water is calm.
The lost hikers were safe once the rescuers found them.

easy.def: A strong box with a lock.
examples: The jewels were locked in a safe.
Dad keeps papers in a safe.
The safe has a secret number.

more.def: A strong metal box with a lock, used to keep valuable things.
examples: The bank keeps gold coins in a big metal safe.
Only my grandmother knows the code that opens the safe.
The treasure was locked in an old safe in the attic.

easy.def: Without harm.
examples: We got home safely.
The boat landed safely.
Cross the street safely.

more.def: In a way that keeps you from harm.
examples: We arrived home safely.
The plane landed safely.
Look both ways to cross the street safely.

easy.def: Being safe from harm.
examples: Wear a helmet for safety.
Safety first!
The safety of children.

more.def: The state of being safe from danger or harm.
examples: A helmet is important for safety.
The lifeguard checks the safety of swimmers.
The firefighters led us to safety.

easy.def: A big piece of cloth on a boat that catches the wind.
examples: The boat has a white sail.
The wind filled the sail.
The sail is up.

more.def: A large piece of strong cloth fixed to a boat that catches the wind to push it along.
examples: The wind filled the white sail.
A sail is raised on the boat's tall mast.
The sailors lowered the sail when the storm came.

easy.def: To travel on water in a boat.
examples: We sail on the lake.
The ship sailed away.
They sailed across the sea.

more.def: To travel across water in a boat, especially a sailboat.
examples: We sailed across the lake on Saturday.
The ship sailed out of the harbor at dawn.
She sailed all the way around the island.

easy.def: A person who works on a ship.
examples: The sailor sailed the ship.
A sailor wore a blue hat.
Sailors work on boats.

more.def: A person who works on a ship or sails a boat.
examples: The sailor climbed the mast.
Sailors pulled the ropes.
The sailor sailed across the sea.

easy.def: A reason for doing something.
examples: We hurried for the sake of the baby.
Be careful for your own sake.
He stayed for his friend's sake.

more.def: The good or benefit of someone or something.
examples: For the sake of the sleeping baby, we whispered.
She walked slowly for her grandmother's sake.
Do it for your own sake.

easy.def: A dish of cold vegetables.
examples: I eat salad.
The salad has lettuce and tomatoes.
Dad made a salad.

more.def: A dish made from raw vegetables or fruit, often mixed with a dressing.
examples: Dinner included a salad of lettuce and tomatoes.
She tossed the salad with oil and vinegar.
We made a fruit salad with grapes and apples.

easy.def: A small animal like a lizard that lives near water.
examples: A salamander lives in the pond.
The salamander is slimy.
I found a salamander.

more.def: A small animal with a long tail and smooth, damp skin that looks like a lizard and lives near water.
examples: A salamander crawled under the wet log.
The salamander has smooth, damp skin.
We found a salamander beside the stream.

easy.def: A spicy sausage that is cut into thin slices.
examples: I ate a salami sandwich.
Salami is spicy.
He put salami on the pizza.

more.def: A large, spicy sausage that is cut into thin slices and eaten cold in sandwiches or on pizza.
examples: Dad made me a sandwich with cheese and salami.
The deli cut the salami into thin slices.
She put salami and olives on the pizza.

easy.def: Money you get for doing a job.
examples: Dad gets a salary.
The salary is paid each month.
Her salary is good.

more.def: A fixed amount of money that a person gets for their work, usually paid every month.
examples: Mom gets her salary at the end of each month.
The teacher's salary pays for their home.
The job has a good salary.

easy.def: Selling something.
examples: The sale of the house.
The store made a sale.
The sale of the toy.

more.def: The act of selling something.
examples: The sale of the old house took a month.
The store made a big sale today.
We held a bake sale.

easy.def: A time when things cost less.
examples: There is a sale at the shoe store.
The toys are on sale.
Coats are on sale.

more.def: A time when a shop sells things at lower prices.
examples: There is a sale at the shoe store this weekend.
Winter boots are on sale this week.
Winter coats go on sale in March.

easy.def: A man whose job is to sell things.
examples: The salesman sold us a car.
A salesman knocked on the door.
The salesman had a smile.

more.def: A man whose job is to sell things to customers.
examples: The salesman showed us a new car.
A salesman came to the door with a vacuum cleaner.
The salesman explained how the machine worked.

easy.def: The wet stuff in your mouth, also called spit.
examples: Saliva helps you chew.
Saliva is in your mouth.
Your mouth makes saliva.

more.def: The clear liquid in your mouth that helps you chew and swallow food.
examples: Saliva makes the food in your mouth soft so it is easy to swallow.
Your mouth waters when you smell a lemon because it makes more saliva.
Saliva starts to break down food as you chew.

easy.def: A large fish that swims up rivers.
examples: The salmon swims upstream.
We ate salmon.
A salmon jumped.

more.def: A large fish that is pink inside and swims from the sea up rivers to lay eggs.
examples: The salmon swam upstream to lay its eggs.
We had grilled salmon for dinner.
Bears catch salmon in the river.

easy.def: A shop for hair care.
examples: Mom went to the salon.
The salon is fancy.
The salon cuts hair.

more.def: A shop where people go to have their hair cut and styled.
examples: Mom had her hair cut at the salon.
The salon smelled of shampoo.
The hair salon was busy.

easy.def: A white powder that makes food taste better.
examples: I put salt on my eggs.
The soup needs salt.
Salt is in the shaker.

more.def: A white mineral in tiny grains that is used to flavor food.
examples: She sprinkled salt on the popcorn.
Ocean water is full of salt.
Add a pinch of salt to the soup.

easy.def: Tasting of salt.
examples: The soup is salty.
I like salty chips.
The sea water is salty.

more.def: Tasting of salt, or containing a lot of salt.
examples: The pretzels were so salty that I needed a drink of water.
Ocean water is salty, so you cannot drink it.
The salty air at the beach made my lips taste of salt.

easy.def: To show respect with a hand movement.
examples: The soldier saluted.
I salute the flag.
He saluted the captain.

more.def: To raise your hand to your forehead to show respect.
examples: The soldiers saluted the flag.
He saluted the captain as she walked by.
The scouts saluted at the ceremony.

easy.def: To save something from being lost or thrown away.
examples: We tried to salvage the toy.
Dad can salvage the old table.
They salvaged wood from the barn.

more.def: To rescue or save something from damage, loss or a wreck so that it can be used again.
examples: Divers salvaged gold coins from the sunken ship.
We salvaged some good boards from the old fence.
She tried to salvage the cake after it broke in half.

easy.def: Things that are saved from a wreck or fire.
examples: The salvage is on the boat.
We sell salvage from old houses.
Workers sorted the salvage.

more.def: Things that are rescued from a wreck or from a ruined place so that they can be used again.
examples: The salvage from the old ship was sold at the dock.
The company reuses the salvage from torn-down buildings.
Divers brought up salvage from the bottom of the lake.

easy.def: Being saved.
examples: The boat was our salvation.
The rain was salvation.
Salvation came at last.

more.def: The act of being saved from danger or harm.
examples: The lifeboat was our salvation.
The rain was a salvation for the dry fields.
The stranded sailors found salvation.

easy.def: Just like another.
examples: We have the same hat.
They are the same size.
I ate the same lunch.

more.def: Exactly alike, or not different in any way.
examples: The twins wore the same coat to school.
Two plus two is the same as one plus three.
We go to the same park every Saturday.

easy.def: A small part to show what something is like.
examples: We tried a sample of cheese.
The shop gave out samples.
She took a sample of the water.

more.def: A small amount of something that shows what the rest is like.
examples: The grocery store gave out free samples of cheese.
The scientist took a water sample from the lake.
He showed a sample of the paint color.

easy.def: A fighter from long ago in Japan.
examples: A samurai wore armor.
We read a book about a samurai.
The samurai bowed politely.

more.def: A soldier from long ago in Japan who followed a strict code of honor and often wore special armor.
examples: The samurai in the story followed a code of honor and bravery.
Museums in Japan show the armor and swords of samurai from long ago.
A samurai was expected to be loyal and polite as well as strong.

easy.def: A safe place.
examples: The park is a sanctuary for birds.
My room is my sanctuary.
The sanctuary keeps animals safe.

more.def: A place that is safe, where people or animals are protected from harm.
examples: The park is a sanctuary for hundreds of birds.
Her quiet room was a sanctuary where she could read in peace.
The wildlife sanctuary gives hurt animals a safe home until they are well.

easy.def: Tiny bits of rock that cover a beach.
examples: We built a castle in the sand.
The sand is hot.
I have sand in my shoes.

more.def: A mass of tiny grains of rock found on beaches and in deserts.
examples: The children dug in the warm sand.
Wind blew the sand into piles in the desert.
Sand got into my shoes at the beach.

easy.def: A make-believe man who puts sand in your eyes to make you sleepy.
examples: The sandman made me sleepy.
Here comes the sandman.
In the story, the sandman came.

more.def: A make-believe character in stories who sprinkles sand in children's eyes at night to help them fall asleep.
examples: In the old story, the sandman visits children at night and sprinkles sleepy sand in their eyes.
Dad said the sandman was coming, so it was time for bed.
The song asks the sandman to bring a dream.

easy.def: Two slices of bread with food in between.
examples: I ate a sandwich.
Peanut butter sandwich.
Mom made a sandwich.

more.def: Two slices of bread with food such as meat, cheese or jam between them.
examples: I packed a cheese sandwich for lunch.
She made a peanut butter sandwich.
Dad cut the sandwich in half.

easy.def: Covered with sand.
examples: The beach is sandy.
My feet are sandy.
The path was sandy.

more.def: Covered with sand, or like sand.
examples: We walked on the sandy beach.
My feet were sandy after the swim.
The path was soft and sandy.

easy.def: Having a healthy, clear mind.
examples: A sane person would not do that.
The plan was sane.
He seemed calm and sane.

more.def: Thinking in a clear, sensible way.
examples: A sane person would not jump off the roof.
The plan sounded sane and safe.
Everyone around him stayed calm and sane.

easy.def: Having a clear, calm mind.
examples: He kept his sanity.
Sleep helps your sanity.
She tried to keep her sanity.

more.def: The ability to think clearly and sensibly, with a calm and healthy mind.
examples: After a long day of noise, a quiet walk helped me keep my sanity.
A good night's sleep helps you keep your sanity during a busy week.
Counting slowly to ten helped her keep her sanity while the baby cried.

easy.def: The sweet liquid inside a tree or plant.
examples: Sap runs in the tree.
Maple sap is sweet.
Sap dripped from the tree.

more.def: The watery liquid inside plants and trees that carries food to every part.
examples: Maple syrup is made by boiling the sap of maple trees.
Sticky sap oozed from the cut in the pine tree.
In spring, the sap starts to rise in the trees.

easy.def: Saying the opposite of what you mean, to be funny or unkind.
examples: Her sarcasm made us laugh.
He said it with sarcasm.
Sarcasm can hurt.

more.def: Saying the opposite of what you mean, often in a joking or unkind way, as in saying "Great weather!" in the pouring rain.
examples: "Great weather!" he said with sarcasm as the rain poured down.
Her sarcasm made everyone laugh, though some people did not get the joke.
Sarcasm is hard to understand when you cannot hear someone's voice.

easy.def: Saying the opposite of what you mean to be funny.
examples: He gave a sarcastic reply.
She sounded sarcastic.
That was a sarcastic joke.

more.def: Saying the opposite of what you really mean, often in a joking way that can sound unkind.
examples: When it started to pour, Dad made a sarcastic joke about the nice weather.
Her sarcastic voice showed that she did not really think the idea was great.
Try not to be sarcastic with a friend who is feeling sad.

easy.def: A small silver fish, often in cans.
examples: I ate a sardine.
Sardines are small fish.
A sardine is silver.

more.def: A small, silvery fish that is often packed tightly in cans.
examples: A cat ate a sardine from the can.
Sardines swim in big groups in the sea.
We were packed in the bus like sardines in a can.

easy.def: Bold and a little rude in a funny way.
examples: The sassy parrot talked back.
She gave a sassy answer.
Our sassy puppy barked at us.

more.def: Bold, lively and a bit cheeky, often in a way that is funny but not always polite.
examples: The sassy parrot copied everything we said and squawked back at us.
She gave a sassy reply and then grinned.
Her sassy hat had a big purple feather on top.

easy.def: A machine that circles Earth in space.
examples: A satellite is in the sky.
The satellite takes pictures of Earth.
We watch TV by satellite.

more.def: A machine sent into space to circle Earth and send back pictures or signals.
examples: A weather satellite took pictures of the storm from space.
Satellites help phones and maps find where you are.
The satellite circles Earth once every ninety minutes.

easy.def: A moon or small body that goes around a planet.
examples: The moon is a satellite.
Earth has one satellite.
Jupiter has many satellites.

more.def: A natural body, such as a moon, that travels in a path around a larger planet.
examples: The moon is Earth's natural satellite.
Jupiter has dozens of small satellites circling around it.
Scientists use telescopes to study the satellites of Saturn.

easy.def: A smooth, shiny cloth.
examples: The ribbon is satin.
She wore a satin dress.
The pillow is made of satin.

more.def: A smooth, shiny cloth that is soft to the touch, often used for dresses and ribbons.
examples: The gown was made of shiny satin that slid easily through my fingers.
She tied a satin ribbon in her hair.
The cushion was covered with red satin.

easy.def: A happy feeling when you have what you want.
examples: I felt satisfaction when I finished.
She smiled with satisfaction.
He took satisfaction in his work.

more.def: A pleased feeling that you get when you have done well or have what you need.
examples: I felt satisfaction when I finished the puzzle.
She smiled with satisfaction after a good meal.
He took satisfaction in a job well done.

easy.def: Good enough.
examples: Her work was satisfactory.
The room was satisfactory.
The food was satisfactory.

more.def: Good enough to meet what is needed, though not wonderful.
examples: My teacher said my story was satisfactory but that I could add more detail.
The old tent was satisfactory for one night of camping.
We found a satisfactory place to put the new bookshelf.

easy.def: Happy with what you got.
examples: I am satisfied with my work.
She felt satisfied.
The customer was satisfied.

more.def: Pleased because you have what you need or want.
examples: I am satisfied with my score.
She felt satisfied after a big dinner.
The customer was satisfied with the new shoes.

easy.def: To give someone what they need.
examples: The snack satisfied me.
The meal will satisfy us.
She satisfied her hunger.

more.def: To give someone enough of what they want or need so that they are content.
examples: A big sandwich will satisfy my hunger.
The answer did not satisfy the teacher.
The meal satisfied everyone.

easy.def: Giving you a happy, full feeling.
examples: It was a satisfying meal.
Finishing the puzzle was satisfying.
A satisfying nap.

more.def: Giving you a feeling of happiness or fullness because it is what you wanted or needed.
examples: After a long hike, a hot meal is very satisfying.
Finishing the huge puzzle was a satisfying end to the rainy day.
The popping of the bubble wrap is oddly satisfying.

easy.def: The day after Friday.
examples: We play on Saturday.
Saturday is the weekend.
I sleep late on Saturday.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Friday and before Sunday.
examples: We go to the market on Saturday.
There is no school on Saturday.
My soccer game is on Saturday morning.

easy.def: A thick liquid that you put on food.
examples: I like tomato sauce.
The sauce is on the pasta.
Dad made a sauce.

more.def: A thick liquid that is poured over food to give it flavor.
examples: Mom poured tomato sauce on the spaghetti.
The pizza had a lot of cheese and sauce.
Dip your fries in the sauce.

easy.def: A small cooking pot with a handle.
examples: Mom heated the soup in a saucepan.
The saucepan is hot.
The saucepan has a lid.

more.def: A deep cooking pot with a long handle and often a lid.
examples: He boiled the eggs in a small saucepan.
The saucepan is on the stove.
He stirred the sauce in the saucepan.

easy.def: A small plate that goes under a cup.
examples: The cup is on a saucer.
She held the saucer.
Put the cup on the saucer.

more.def: A small, shallow dish that is placed under a cup.
examples: The cup sat on a small saucer.
She held the cup and saucer in her hands.
A drop of milk spilled onto the saucer.

easy.def: A round flying object in stories about visitors from space.
examples: A flying saucer is in the story.
The saucer landed.
The toy saucer is silver.

more.def: A round flying machine in stories, usually from outer space.
examples: In the story, a silver saucer landed in the field.
The toy saucer spun and glowed.
The movie had a flying saucer and a friendly alien.

easy.def: A tube of seasoned chopped meat.
examples: I eat a sausage.
The sausage is hot.
We had sausages for breakfast.

more.def: A food made of chopped meat and spices that are packed into a tube-shaped skin.
examples: I had a sausage for breakfast.
The sausages sizzled on the grill.
He sliced the sausage into rounds.

easy.def: Wild and fierce.
examples: The savage storm blew.
A savage beast growled.
The savage waves hit the shore.

more.def: Very fierce, wild and cruel.
examples: The savage storm tore the sails.
The savage wolf growled in the story.
Savage waves crashed against the cliffs.

easy.def: To keep safe from harm.
examples: The dog saved the boy.
Save the bird.
He saved a cat.

more.def: To keep a person or thing safe from harm or loss.
examples: The lifeguard saved the swimmer who was tired.
Firefighters saved the kitten from the tall tree.
Planting trees can help save the forest.

easy.def: To keep something to use later.
examples: I save my money.
Save me a seat.
She saves old boxes.

more.def: To keep money or things so that you can use them later.
examples: I am saving my coins to buy a new bike.
Save some cake for your sister.
We saved the leftover soup for lunch tomorrow.

easy.def: Money you keep and do not spend.
examples: I put it in my savings.
The savings are in the bank.
Her savings are growing.

more.def: Money that you have put away and not spent.
examples: I put my allowance in my savings.
The savings are in a jar.
She used her savings to buy a bike.

easy.def: A person who rescues someone from danger.
examples: The firefighter was our savior.
She was the savior.
He is the savior of the village.

more.def: A person who saves someone or something from danger or trouble.
examples: The firefighter was our savior when the kitchen caught fire.
In the story, a brave girl became the savior of her village.
The kind stranger was my savior when I lost my way.

easy.def: To speak words out loud.
examples: Say hello to Grandpa.
She said her name.
The sign says stop.

more.def: To speak words aloud, or to show something in writing.
examples: Please say your name and your favorite food to the class.
The recipe says to bake the cookies for ten minutes.
He said that he would be late for dinner.
